newsitem.title: GUAM: No more survivors from KAL crash - U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: No more survivors from KAL crash - U.S. official.

text.p: A U.S. Navy official involved in the rescue effort for a crashed Korean Air Lines jetliner said on Wednesday that he believed there was no one left alive at the scene of the fiery crash.
Navy Admiral Martin Janczak said: "We have search and rescue dogs available to us, but it's our opinion that no one is still alive."
He told a news conference that 30 people had survived and were now in hospital, with 69 bodies recovered and 155 people still missing.
There were 231 passengers and 23 crewmembers on the Boeing 747, which crashed into a hillside near Guam's main airport overnight.
